*   **Transition Region:** If the opacity fall-off is not inversely proportional to the gradient magnitude, the transition region thickness will vary, leading to visual inconsistencies [S2, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that 'The best results are obtained when the thickness of the transition region is constant throughout the volume' and that this can be 'approximated by having the opacity fall off at a rate inversely proportional to the magnitude of the local gradient vector.' The claim posits that if this condition is not met, the thickness will vary. Since the evidence establishes the inverse proportionality as the method to achieve constant thickness, the logical contrapositive (that failing to do so leads to varying thickness) is supported by the text.
